nodes.label: Layer 1 - refused by code
nodes.rationale: The only layer enforced mechanically. Nothing here needs judgment: run `run_matrix.py --preflight-only --tasks <task_id>` and read the output. Offline, no credentials, no spend; needs Docker and, the first time a repo is mirrored, network. The asymmetry that sets the bar: a refused task costs a message, an accepted-wrongly task costs a matrix -- every arm scored on an unverifiable guess, in an append-only log.

nodes.label: Layer 2 - required, and nothing checks it
nodes.rationale: Where a task set goes wrong quietly: every item produces a task that passes Layer 1 and measures the wrong thing. Covers the oracle (behaviour not internals, no property-based suites, determinism), provenance (base_sha, verbatim reference, licence), the prompt (verbatim, no replayed human corrections), and the image (no submodules, no VCS-derived version, suite fast enough).

nodes.label: Layer 3 - properties of the set, not of any task
nodes.rationale: ~80 harvested to land ~60 (section 3.5), stratified to the MEASURED production distribution rather than a guessed split -- a 50/50 split on a workload that is 70% small edits measures the wrong thing and will not transfer to the bill. Must include a long-session stratum because all three candidates claim 256K context, degrade unevenly well before it, and small tasks never surface that.

nodes.label: Tests assert behaviour, not internal names
nodes.rationale: The single most important judgment call per candidate, and no gate catches it. click #3678 was rejected for exactly this: its tests pin an arbitrary storage name, so a different-but-correct fix would be scored as a failure. Prefer tests that compare rendered output, return values, or raised messages.

nodes.label: No property-based oracle
nodes.rationale: A hypothesis-driven suite can pass a wrong fix on a lucky draw and fail a right one on an unlucky seed; attrs and cattrs are excluded for this. The suite must also be deterministic -- preflight runs p2p twice, so a flake makes the gate a coin flip and the eval unreproducible.

nodes.label: base_sha is merge_commit^1
nodes.rationale: The real parent of the merge, not the PR's recorded base.sha. The base branch advances between a PR being opened and merged, and diffing against the stale one puts unrelated commits into the reference. Measured on click #3434: 7c99ebe -> 63274a7.

nodes.label: The reference is the real merged PR, verbatim
nodes.rationale: Section 3.2, without exception. It converts the judge's question from open-ended 'is this diff good?' (kappa ~ 0.32, below the 0.6 acceptability bar) into reference-anchored 'does this accomplish what the reference accomplished?'. The licence must permit redistributing the diff and the prompt.

nodes.label: The prompt is verbatim
nodes.rationale: Section 3.3: the issue title, then the issue body exactly as filed, plus the ticket description where one exists. Nothing added -- a harness-authored sentence ('the tests are in tests/', 'do not edit the tests') makes it a different task from the one a human actually opened, and this eval exists to measure the workflow that happens rather than a tidied one. Human corrections are not replayed because a follow-up like 'fix the import on line 40' was conditioned on the original model's output and is incoherent against a candidate that wrote different code.

nodes.label: rubric_items from unreplayed human corrections
nodes.rationale: Human follow-up turns that cannot be replayed become rubric_items instead -- a free, human-authored list of what 'done' required.

nodes.label: Three silent task-image build failures
nodes.rationale: All found by screening rather than reasoning. (1) No git submodules -- the build context is `git archive base_sha`, which drops them, so tomlkit cannot collect its suite. (2) No VCS-derived version unless build: supplies a pretend-version -- git archive leaves no .git and setuptools_scm refuses; measured across 12 candidates only setuptools_scm is strict, hatch-vcs builds fine. (3) The suite must be fast enough: preflight runs it four times under a 600 s timeout and the agent re-runs it inside wall_clock_timeout_s, so ~40 s is the practical ceiling and click's 1.4 s is what comfortable looks like.

nodes.label: Pruned run tree shortens the abbreviated SHA
nodes.rationale: Tags that are ancestors of base_sha survive the prune, so `git describe` still resolves and setuptools_scm/hatch-vcs can still derive a version. But core.abbrev auto-sizes to the smaller object count, so 8.3.3-69-g63274a79 becomes 8.3.3-69-g63274a7 (measured) -- a package installed at image-build time and one the agent rebuilds in the run tree disagree on version string. Nothing asserts this; preflight already runs the suite inside the image, so a mismatch that breaks anything surfaces there.

nodes.label: The model-neutral drop rule
nodes.rationale: Drop only if ALL four models score 0% (floor -- usually underspecified rather than hard) or ALL four score 100% (ceiling -- no signal). Keep every disagreement, however lopsided: a task only Sonnet solves is among the most informative in the set. Read against the measured variance: on 2026-08-13 this task set's one task went 4/4 resolved and then 2/4 on the same four arms hours apart at temperature 1.0 and N=1 -- between-run variance larger than the between-arm spread. At N=3 a discriminating task can present as a floor, which is an argument for more repeats in the pilot, not for a looser drop rule.

nodes.label: Calibration pilot before freeze
nodes.rationale: All four models, N=3, across every candidate. Selecting tasks by one model's difficulty curve tilts the set toward what that model happens to discriminate on, which is precisely the bias this eval exists to avoid.

nodes.label: task_version bumps on any edit
nodes.rationale: It is not part of run_id, so an edited task leaves every finished cell looking complete while mixing two different tasks under one task_id. Resume hard-refuses on the mismatch, per cell.

nodes.label: Screened repository list
nodes.rationale: Measured 2026-08-13 in python:3.12-slim-bookworm: editable install, git clean -xfd, full suite, then git status. Suite times are at HEAD, NOT at any candidate's base_sha -- green here does not guarantee green there, and preflight remains the gate. The PR column counts merged PRs linked to an issue created after 2024-01-01 and is an availability proxy only. Excluded: tomlkit (submodule dropped by git archive), attrs/cattrs (hypothesis suites plus a site-packages `attr` collision), python-slugify (no harvestable PRs).

nodes.label: sqlglot base_sha date constraint
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md was added 2026-02-02 (a65c8701a306, PR #6899) and AGENTS.md followed 2026-03-19 (7f0dd47f60a3), with a later commit making CLAUDE.md a symlink to it. Both are present at HEAD and preflight's `test -e` follows symlinks, so base_sha must predate 2026-02-02. That leaves 680 clean candidates against 116 after the cutoff -- the constraint costs almost nothing and sqlglot remains the richest source by an order of magnitude. A SQL transpiler is also close to the ideal bug shape: input SQL, exact expected output, tests that assert rendered strings rather than internal names.

nodes.label: Pinned reference.diff cut flags
nodes.rationale: `git -c diff.noprefix=false -c diff.renames=true diff --binary <base_sha> <merge_commit>`. Not cosmetic: without them the diff's SHAPE is a property of the harvester's ~/.gitconfig rather than of the task, and 80 references cut on different machines would not be the same kind of object. noprefix=false because a --no-prefix diff is refused at load (git apply's -p1 would strip a REAL path component and silently swap which files are the oracle); renames=true because `copies` turns plain modifications into copy chunks; --binary because a plain git diff renders a binary change as 'Binary files ... differ' with no payload, which loads clean and then fails in preflight. Leave core.quotepath at its default -- quoted headers are never parsed for paths, and turning it off writes raw non-UTF-8 bytes that fail to decode at load.

nodes.label: Cutting one - the harvest procedure
nodes.rationale: Read the tests FIRST -- Layer 2's behaviour-not-internals rule disqualifies most candidates and is cheapest to check before anything else. Leave repo.start_sha out on the first pass and pin the value the gate reports. Run the f2p tests by hand at the start state to get node ids right -- they are measured, never guessed. Iterate --preflight-only until it prints PASS, because every problem it reports maps to a defect that would otherwise read as model capability.

nodes.label: src/bakeoff/tasks.py loader rules
nodes.rationale: Runs before anything builds. Enforces: base_sha is 40 hex and resolves; a declared start_sha equals the recomputed one; prompt non-empty; tests.paths non-empty (it is what splits reference.diff); tests.f2p non-empty, duplicate-free and disjoint from p2p; reference.diff begins with `diff --git` with nothing before it; both halves non-empty after the split; no rename crosses the test/solution boundary; task_id unique in the set, because run_id is sha256(task|model|sample|attempt) and two tasks sharing an id collide in the event log -- discovered at the far end of a matrix, after the tokens are spent.

nodes.label: src/bakeoff/preflight.py checks
nodes.rationale: Runs inside the pinned image, before the proxy starts. Requires pytest in tests.runner (the red/green distinction is built on pytest exit codes and nothing else can supply it), a non-root image, claude --version matching the base pin, git and rg present, HEAD at start_sha, and NO CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.claude/.cursorrules in the start state. f2p must exit exactly 1 at the start state -- not 0 (already solved), not 2/4/5 (broken environment) -- and every declared f2p id must appear in pytest's FAILED/ERROR lines, because `returncode != 0` accepts a broken environment as evidence the bug is present, which is the Phase 0c failure. p2p exits 0 at the start state, git status is clean after the suite runs, the solution half applies cleanly, and after the reference fix f2p exits 0 with p2p still 0.
